newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE awards deals for $114 mln northern power grid.
newsitem.headline: UAE awards deals for $114 mln northern power grid.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates has awarded contracts worth 420 million dirhams ($114 million) to set up a power grid in the northern emirates, an electricity and water ministry official said in remarks published on Thursday.

"One contract, valued at 260 million dirhams, is for the setting up of five power stations, while another 160 million dirham contract has been signed to supply overhead towers, cables and wires," ministry undersecretary Saeed Majid al-Shamsi was quoted by the Gulf News daily as saying.

He said the first contract with Hyundai involves the setting up of two power stations in Ras Al Khaimah, one each in Umm Al Quwain and Ajman and another in Dhaid in Sharjah. The five stations should be completed within 18 months.
The second contract was signed with Sim-Al Rustomani Co.
Shamsi said the ministry would sign another contract with a U.S. firm for the second phase of the grid in the northern emirates, inclucing connections with the eastern region.
Shamsi said the project would be an important step towards the proposed setting up of a Gulf-wide electricity grid.
Demand for electricity has grown faster in the Gulf in the past 20 years than in any other region in the world, experts say. Demand in the UAE shot up 40 percent in the past five years.
